checks.claim: Hooks load code from the mutable clone path (unpinned).
checks.evidence: README.md:116-117 says 'Claude Code, Codex, the Copilot CLI and opencode run the plugin from the clone, so leave it in place'. README.md:199 says to update by `git pull` in the clone. On Windows the lib symlink (git ls-files mode 120000) checks out as a stub. te_bootstrap.py:98-118 then misses in the install copy and falls through to the known_marketplaces.json or config.toml source, which is the user's clone (te_bootstrap.py:57-95). This applies on this user's Windows machine.

missed_issues: Repository code can run inside TE's own detached processes, outside the agent's permission system, with default settings. context.py:84-93 starts every detached job (fold at every SessionEnd and for pending sessions at SessionStart, judge, repomap, migrate, the apply-pending waiter) as `python -m tokeneconomizer.plugin.cli` with cwd=repo root, and no -P, -I or PYTHONSAFEPATH (grep finds none). `python -m` puts the cwd first on sys.path, ahead of PYTHONPATH. So a repository-root random.py, json.py, glob.py, argparse.py, copy.py, email/, html/ or tokeneconomizer/ is imported and executed with the hook's full environment. fold.py imports tempfile, which imports random; cli.py imports toolcheck, which imports http.server. I checked the Python behavior with my own test files: a cwd random.py ran under `python -m` with PYTHONPATH set. On Windows the WMI path does the same (winspawn.py:88). This bears directly on OAW's ingest workflow: if TE is installed user-wide, opening an untrusted candidate clone in Claude Code would execute candidate code. Even benign repositories with a random.py or json.py at the root would silently break TE's folding.

On Windows, the Codex hook (codex-hooks.json commandWindows) uses `python -c`, which also puts the cwd at sys.path[0] for every hook, including every PostToolUse. If Codex runs hooks in the project directory, this is the same shadowing risk on the synchronous hook path. That depends on Codex's hook cwd, which I could not verify statically.

Claude side calls (judge, nudge writer, proposer, toolprune measure) do not disable the user's other hooks or plugins: no `--settings {"disableAllHooks":true}`, no --bare (grep confirms). With claude-mem installed (also under evaluation here), every TE judge call becomes a nested headless Claude session that claude-mem's SessionStart, PostToolUse and SessionEnd hooks observe, record and inject into. That adds cost and pollutes memory. The digest's 'cheap nested evaluation calls' nutrient inherits this gap.

--strict-mcp-config/empty --mcp-config and --no-session-persistence are added only if `claude --help` lists them (sidecall.py:183-214). On a CLI that lacks them, side calls load all MCP servers (TE's own note: about 570k vs 14k effective tokens with 31 servers) and appear in the user's resume history.

The loopguard judge digest is not just 'command templates'. loopguard/state.py:186-187 sends the first 90 characters of each raw bash command, plus grep patterns, edited basenames and hashed error signatures, to the provider (state.py:214-232). Inline secrets in commands, such as `curl -H 'Authorization: ...'` or `export TOKEN=...`, would go to the judge model. PLUGIN.md:548-551 overstates the masking.

On Codex, side calls run on the user's default Codex model (sidecall.py:476,487; paid_model empty by default), not a cheap model. Combined with the ~25k base prompt, the default-on judge can be more expensive there than on Claude, where it uses haiku.

The loopguard has a judge-free backstop redirect: a turn past envelope × backstop_mult gets the template redirect without any model call (loopguard/turn.py:332-343). 'A judge model decides' is not the only path.

Even with every mechanism off, the six hooks still start sh + Python on every tool call and session event. Only uninstalling or disabling the plugin removes that latency, so OAW latency_ms A/B arms with TE installed but 'off' are not clean.

`te probe` (Copilot, explicit command only) creates its throwaway repository inside a folder the user's Copilot trusts and runs `copilot -p --allow-all-tools` there (probe.py:1-22,118-121). It is opt-in, but it writes into a user-trusted location.

The digest's EGM risk is narrower and has mitigations it does not mention. The plugin will not edit a git-tracked .codex/config.toml (denylist.py:420-425), it rolls back if `codex features list` rejects the edit (denylist.py:440-446), and collaboration is proposed only if it was never used in that repository (toolprune/codex.py:515-566). If OAW commits a project .codex/config.toml, TE cannot touch it.
integration_mode_note: I agree with absorb_method; the case against packing or bundling is stronger than the digest says. On top of the hooks, the default auto writes to .claude/.codex settings, the detached daemons and the second model runtime, I found two more problems. Every detached TE job runs `python -m` with the repository root first on sys.path (context.py:84-93), so repository-root modules execute outside the agent's permission system. Claude side calls also leave other plugins' hooks running, claude-mem included. Corrections for the absorbed methods: (a) cite pricing.py:135-160 for the hard-fail on unknown model ids; the plugin's accounting.py actually falls back silently. (b) Any nested `claude -p` grader recipe OAW adopts should also pass `--settings '{\"disableAllHooks\":true}'` (or equivalent) and treat a missing --strict-mcp-config or --no-session-persistence as an error, not silently drop the flag. (c) Any OAW subprocess that runs in a candidate or user repository should use `python -I` or `-P`. The v2.0.0-execution.md:78 'mandatory nudge' line refers to the Hermes branch's nudge and usage counters, so it only weakly matches TE's loop redirect. The stronger conflicts are 'second model runtime' and 'background ... daemon' on the same line, and Skill_Guide.md:17 (no silent .claude edits). TE does not address the user's graphify or vector data-map wish: grep finds no embedding, vector or graph store, and repomap is aider's tree-sitter/PageRank text map, off by default.
